resources.string: Your Robot and the Robots of people you pair with can ask each other things, like a time to meet. End-to-end encrypted, with no Robot server in between.

You pick a mode each time you pair. Anonymous: neither network learns who talks to whom, but it\'s slower and uses more battery. Private: faster, and goes direct on the same network, but a push server sees that your phones talk.
Sent only to Robots you pair with, when you pair. One line, up to 40 characters.
Use one line of up to 40 characters.

Unpair everyone and delete Robot to Robot\'s keys
Robot unpairs everyone you\'re paired with and deletes Robot to Robot\'s keys. To pair again, each of you makes a new pairing.
Robot to Robot\'s keys or saved data can\'t be read. Start over, then pair again with each person.
Delete Robot to Robot\'s keys and everything it saved on this phone

Robot can\'t reach anyone from here, so no one is told. It deletes Robot to Robot\'s keys and everything it saved on this phone. Each person stays paired with you on their phone until they unpair. To pair again, each of you makes a new pairing. If you use a push app, it keeps what Robot registered with it until you clear Robot there.

resources.string: Requests waiting, and what Robot handled since yesterday. Only while your phone is unlocked.
Calendars other Robots see as busy
Other Robots see only when you\'re busy, in half hours. Never what, where or with whom.
Robot can\'t read your calendar. Allow it in Settings › People, notes and calendar.

Some networks block Tor: at work, at school, or in another country. A bridge is a way into Tor that isn\'t on its public list, so other Robots can still reach yours. Leave it off unless Robot to Robot can\'t connect.
Tor connects on its own, as it always has. Your network can see that you use Tor.
Tor on its own first. If it can\'t connect within 30 seconds, Snowflake, then the built-in obfs4 bridges, then meek.
Looks like a video call. A volunteer\'s proxy and the Tor Project\'s broker see your address and that you use Snowflake, never whom you reach.
Looks like random bytes. The bridge sees your address, as Tor\'s first relay does without one, never whom you reach.
Only the bridge you enter sees your address. For obfs4, WebTunnel, Snowflake, meek or a plain bridge.
Paste a bridge line from bridges.torproject.org, or one from someone you trust.

Robot can\'t use that as a bridge line. Check it and paste it again.
With Automatic, meek is the last try: a large cloud service sees your address and that you use meek. A change takes effect the next time Tor starts, or at once if it hasn\'t connected yet.
Files kept in step with another Robot, once you both say yes

A shared folder stays in step with one other Robot. Each side says yes once, then new files arrive without asking each time, up to 500 files and 1 GiB a folder. What arrives is locked, sealed and never opened for you. You can leave at any time and keep your copies.
Their Robot asks them first and tells them what joining means. Nothing is shared until they say yes. The name you give the folder is sent to them.
Their Robot is told and nothing more arrives. Files you already have stay in Robot Files, and theirs stay with them.

To add a file, open it in Robot Files and choose Add to a shared folder. Taking a file out removes it from the folder on both sides; each person\'s copy in Robot Files stays. Files the other person took out still count toward the folder\'s limits.
Find a time with up to 7 other people
You organize, your Robot asks each person\'s Robot when they\'re busy, and you pick a time that suits. Each person still says yes or no on their own, and each is paired with you, not with each other.

Each Robot is asked only when its person is busy, never what for. Once you propose a time, everyone still in is told who\'s in, by the name each person chose to show, and how many are out or haven\'t answered. Anyone on an Anonymous pairing isn\'t named or counted.
Based on those who answered and your calendar. Pick one to propose it to everyone.
Based on those who answered. Robot can\'t read your calendar, so check these against it. Pick one to propose it to everyone.
%1$s. Each person\'s Robot asks them, and it goes on your calendar once someone says yes.
Each person\'s Robot is told, and it comes off your calendar.
